hook: A hockey puck glides across ice and seems to coast forever; a box shoved across carpet stops almost at once. For two thousand years people believed moving things need a push to keep moving. They were wrong, and finding out why is the start of all of mechanics.

prereq.q: The net force on an object is
options: the vector sum of all forces on it
a force drawn on its diagram
the force that moves it forward
prereq.why: Add the forces with their signs; the result is the net force.

options: the same speed in the same direction
speeding up at a steady rate
prereq.why: Velocity is a vector; constant means neither size nor direction changes.

options: the viewpoint from which motion is measured
the outline of a free-body diagram
prereq.why: Velocities are measured relative to an observer's frame.

figure.caption: At rest or at constant velocity the forces balance. When they do not, the velocity changes.

chain.cause: The forces on an object add to zero in every direction
chain.effect: the object is in translational equilibrium

chain.cause: The object is in translational equilibrium
chain.effect: its velocity stays constant: at rest stays at rest, moving keeps the same speed and direction

chain.cause: A moving object slows down on Earth
chain.effect: some net force (friction, air) acts on it; with that force removed it would keep going

chain.cause: You view the motion from an accelerating vehicle
chain.effect: objects seem to lurch with no force, because that frame is not inertial; use the ground's frame

ideas: Newton's first law: if the net force on an object is zero, its velocity does not change. Rest is just a velocity of zero.
Translational equilibrium: ΣF = 0. Check each direction separately: ΣFx = 0 and ΣFy = 0. Forces can balance in one direction and not the other.
Inertia is an object's tendency to keep its velocity; mass measures it. Inertia is not a force.
An inertial reference frame is one in which the first law holds: the ground, or a vehicle at constant velocity.

misconception.wrong: A moving object needs a forward force on it to keep moving, so a box sliding at constant speed has a larger push than friction.
misconception.right: Constant velocity means zero net force: the push equals the friction. A larger push would make the box speed up.

summary: Newton's first law: zero net force means constant velocity, including rest. Translational equilibrium is ΣF = 0, checked direction by direction; inertia is a property, not a force; and the law holds in inertial frames, such as the ground.
